To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the B3PW91 method with 30% exact exchange admixture and cc-pwCVTZ-PP/6 -31G** basis sets provides the best agreement between the calculated and the experimental (13)C NMR chemical shifts of Pt(2+) organometal complexes in DMSO.

the NMR chemical shifts of (13)C, (15)N, and (19)F atoms bonded to a heavy- atom center can be calculated reliably using a B3P86 or PBE0 functional and the two-component zero order regular approximation approach.

the B3P86 functional with 30% of exact exchange and the cc-pwCVTZ-PP/6 31G** basis sets augmented with the polarisable continuum model of the solvent provides geometries that are compatible with experimental NMR data in terms of both absolute values and trends for the (13) C NMR shifts in Pt(2+)- and Au(3+)-organometallic and metal complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computationally efficient and accurate method to calculate NMR shielding tensors for transition-metal complexes.
the development of an efficient and accurate computational approach to the NMR chemical shift calculation for a series of transition metal complexes.

the development of a computational protocol for the calculation of the NMR chemical shifts of heavy-atom-containing molecules, which provides results in good agreement with experimental observations and which can serve as a useful tool for the prediction of NMR spectra of compounds for which experimental data are not available.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B3P86/def2-TZVPP/def2-TZZPP approach is the method of choice for the calculation of NMR chemical shifts of the complexes investigated here.
hybrid density functional methods with a moderate exact exchange admixture are able to predict the trends in (13)C NMR chemical shifts in square-planar Pt(2+)- and Au(3+)-containing complexes.

the B3PW91/30% exact exchange admixture method is the most reliable for predicting NMR chemical shifts of (13)C, (15)N, and (31)P nuclei connected to a heavy metal center in square-planar Pt(2+)- and Au(3+)-containing complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the B3PW91 and B3LYP methods using the cc-pwCVQZ-PP/6-pG** basis set with the inclusion of spin-orbit corrections provide a reliable and computationally efficient approach to the prediction of (13)C NMR chemical shifts in the heavy-metal complexes studied in this work.
the B3P86/def2-TZVP method is a good choice for predicting NMR chemical shifts of heavy-metal-containing compounds.
relativistic hybrid density functional methods are capable of providing accurate (13)C chemical shift predictions for Pt(2+) complexes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

hybrid density functional methods are able to reproduce experimental NMR chemical shifts in a reliable manner for heavy transition-metal compounds, and that they can be used to provide accurate estimates of the effects of the solvent, geometry, and relativistic effects.
relativistic effects, especially spin-orbit contributions, play an important role in the calculation of the NMR shielding tensors of transition-metal complexes containing Pt(2+) or Au(3+).

the hybrid density functional methods with a large exact exchange admixture are capable of reproducing the trends in the NMR chemical shifts of heavy-metal complexes, and they are therefore suitable for the study of these systems.
